label: X-01
evidence: docs/diagrams/README.md:12-14 says docs/sealmap/ is 'checked by `sealmap verify` in CI'. docs/sealmap/ does not exist at this revision; .github/workflows/ci.yml never runs `sealmap verify` (only `generate` into $RUNNER_TEMP/.sealmap, with a comment that generated output is never committed); main.rs Cmd::Verify calls seal::verify over topics/lock (check.rs ~360-395), not the generated corpus, which is only compared by `generate --check` (main.rs generate()).
rationale: The README statement is false on every count, so the core documentation defect is real. The consequence (undetected drift in a committed docs/sealmap) is overstated because nothing generated is committed.

label: X-02
evidence: collect.rs:1342-1349 (arg) and 1261-1266 walk closure bodies without binding closure params; origin() at collect.rs:1052-1053 looks names up in the outer env. Reproduced: `pub fn go(client: DbClient, events: Vec<u8>) { events.iter().for_each(|client| client.flush()); }` yields [("sym:cargo app . DbClient#flush().", Exact)]. The untyped case gives Inferred via by_name_only (resolve.rs ~925-937), pinned by tests/extract.rs `loose`.
rationale: A shadowing closure parameter inherits the outer variable's type and mints a false Exact call, which I reproduced. The untyped-parameter guess is labelled Inferred and is intended, but the shadowing case is a real defect.

label: X-03
evidence: contract.rs:121-124 read_rec keeps only is_dir/is_file (DirEntry::file_type does not follow symlinks); contract.rs:151-155 write() does fs::write(dir.join(path)) and follows the link. Reproduced: replaced _README.md in the output dir with a symlink to an outside file; write() reported it Missing and overwrote the outside file with '# sealmap corpus...'.
rationale: I reproduced the write through a symlink to a target outside the output directory. Practical exposure depends on who controls the output directory.

label: X-04
evidence: main.rs:345-375 read_topics_rec includes a .md only if seal::topic_id is Some (the cited line 343 is off); the doc comment at main.rs:345-346 defines topics as '.md files ... with a front-matter `id:`'. check.rs verify loops `let Some(id) = topic_id(text) else { continue }`. A file with no id is by definition not a topic (READMEs and indexes live in the same directory).
rationale: The filtering is documented, deliberate behaviour that defines what a topic is. The scenario needs a malformed topic that other structure gates would catch, so this is not a defect in the code as written.

label: X-05
evidence: main.rs:71-73 documents `--name` as 'defaults to the directory or repo names'; main.rs:288 and 314-319 implement that. CI passes `--name sealmap` (ci.yml:29,56), and README.md:286 tells users to check with the options they signed with. The described failure is wrong: `sealmap verify` never compares _index.json/_model.json (it runs seal::verify), and generated output is not committed.
rationale: This is a documented CLI default, not a hidden leak, and the stated failure path through `verify` does not exist.

label: X-06
evidence: isolate.rs:8-10 itself admits a stack overflow aborts and cannot be caught; collect.rs:42 calls syn::parse_file with no depth bound (MAX_EXPR_DEPTH at collect.rs:30 only guards the walker); lib.rs:146-148 promises 'Never fails'. Reproduced: a file with 200,000 nested parentheses made extract() abort the whole process ('has overflowed its stack ... SIGABRT') with no diagnostic.
rationale: I reproduced the process abort, which contradicts the never-fails contract. The trigger input is pathological, but the defect is real.

label: X-07
evidence: contract.rs:98-101 flags extras as Orphaned only when they are .md files carrying the generated marker, although the doc at contract.rs:75-77 says reserved `_` files are part of the corpus; write() acts only on the report (contract.rs:142-159); emit_model is gated at sealmap-corpus lib.rs:203. Reproduced: wrote a full corpus, then regenerated with emit_model=false. The write report was empty, _model.json still existed, and verify returned clean.
rationale: A stale _model.json survives and verification passes, which I reproduced.

label: X-08
evidence: resolve.rs:856 `Recv::Returned(_) | Recv::Computed(_) | Recv::Unknown => None` assigns None to the local `ty`; it does not return from method(). resolve.rs:857 then returns Some((unresolved_method_id(name), External)), so `?` at resolve.rs:826 does not fire. Under ExternalCalls::All, keeps() (confidence.rs:48-55) keeps it; under the default NonStd, unresolved calls are dropped by documented design (confidence.rs:34-36).
rationale: The finding misreads the match arm: those receivers produce an unresolved External call, not a dropped one.

label: X-09
evidence: sealmap-rust lib.rs:155 filters by include_tests; main.rs:74-76 exposes --tests ('Include tests, examples and benches'); layout.rs documents that build.rs and stray files are not extracted. All of these are documented scope choices.
rationale: This is intended, documented scope, opt-in through a flag, not a defect.

label: X-10
evidence: document.rs:146-149 and 153-155 do hardcode "---\n", and read_rec (contract.rs:125) does not normalise. But sealmap writes the corpus itself with LF (contract.rs:155), and CI states that generated output is never committed (ci.yml:24-25), so git autocrlf does not touch it. Even with CRLF, `have != want` already reports drift (contract.rs:83-84); only the Stale/Modified label differs.
rationale: The premise (a committed, CRLF-converted generated corpus) does not hold for this tool's workflow, and a byte-identity gate correctly flags CRLF files as drift. The orphan miss is real code, but only in that unrealistic setup.
